Q362.body: World War II began in Europe with Germany’s invasion of Poland in September 1939, while major fighting in East Asia had already begun. The conflict drew in countries and colonial populations across the globe. Its history includes the Holocaust, widespread attacks on civilians, enormous displacement, and the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The defeat of the Axis powers in 1945 reshaped international institutions and the balance of world power.

Q8740.body: The Vietnam War grew out of the struggle over Vietnam’s political future after French colonial rule and the country’s division. North Vietnam and its allies fought South Vietnam and its allies, including the United States. Fighting extended into Laos and Cambodia. The war caused immense civilian and military losses, provoked international protest, and ended with the fall of Saigon in 1975. The marker represents one major center of a much wider conflict.

Q8663.body: The Korean War began when North Korean forces crossed the division between North and South Korea in June 1950. A United Nations force led by the United States intervened for the South, while China entered on the North’s side. The fighting devastated the peninsula. An armistice in 1953 stopped most combat but did not establish a final peace treaty.

Q15108645.title: The Higgs boson is discovered
Q15108645.body: On July 4, 2012, CERN’s ATLAS and CMS collaborations announced a new particle consistent with the long-predicted Higgs boson. Later measurements strengthened its identification. The discovery supported the explanation of how certain elementary particles acquire mass and demonstrated the value of experiments built and analyzed by international scientific teams.

sources.title: CERN — The Higgs boson

Q16947045.title: Astronauts return to the Moon’s neighborhood
Q16947045.body: Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026, carrying Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen on a crewed journey around the Moon. The mission returned to Earth on April 10. It tested the Orion spacecraft with people aboard and marked a major step in renewed human lunar exploration. This marker shows the Florida launch site; the flight itself traveled through space.

sources.title: NASA — Artemis II mission and return

Q48780688.body: The international agreement on marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction entered into force on January 17, 2026. Often called the High Seas Treaty, it provides a framework for protecting marine ecosystems beyond national waters, assessing environmental impacts, sharing benefits from marine genetic resources, and supporting scientific capacity. Its entry into force begins implementation; it does not mean that all ocean conservation goals have already been achieved.

sources.title: United Nations — BBNJ Agreement

Q136468555.title: Navi Pillay receives the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize announcement
Q136468555.body: On October 9, 2026, South African jurist Navi Pillay was announced as the recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize. Her career includes international criminal justice and service as United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The announcement places international law, accountability, and human rights at the center of this milestone. The marker identifies Oslo, the announcement location; the award ceremony follows later in the year.

sources.title: United Nations — 2026 Nobel Peace Prize announcement

Q138503695.body: The United States and Israel began strikes against Iran on February 28, 2026, initiating a wider regional war. Iranian attacks, fighting involving other regional actors, and disruption to shipping and energy markets broadened its effects. The conflict remained unresolved as of November 8, 2026. This is an ongoing event: the atlas records its beginning and the verified reporting date, rather than implying a completed outcome.

sources.title: Associated Press — reporting through November 8, 2026

Q140984463.body: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia on August 10, 2026, affecting communities around San José del Palmar and across the region. The event caused damage and created urgent public-health and humanitarian needs. Its significance includes both the earthquake itself and the challenges of reaching affected communities and restoring essential services.

sources.title: PAHO — Colombia earthquake public-health assessment

Q140119396.body: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck near Sarangani in the southern Philippines on June 8, 2026. The earthquake and associated tsunami risk affected communities in and around Mindanao. Government disaster reports document evacuation, damage assessment, and relief operations. The marker represents the earthquake region, rather than every community affected.

sources.title: Philippines DSWD — June 2026 earthquake situation report

Q140735282.body: An earthquake struck the Kumamoto region of Japan on July 28, 2026. Japan’s earthquake authorities reported a magnitude of 7.1 and severe local shaking; magnitude estimates differ between agencies and scales. The mainshock and aftershocks prompted emergency response and scientific investigation of the rupture. This entry uses the Japanese government’s event assessment.

sources.title: Japan Earthquake Research Committee — Kumamoto assessment

Q81068910.title: COVID-19 becomes a global pandemic
Q81068910.body: On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization characterized COVID-19 as a pandemic. The spread of SARS-CoV-2 caused a global health emergency and disrupted work, education, travel, and daily life. The response included public-health measures, rapid scientific collaboration, and the development of vaccines. The marker identifies WHO headquarters in Geneva, not the geographical origin or full extent of the outbreak.

sources.title: WHO — Timeline of the COVID-19 response

Q110999040.title: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine
Q110999040.body: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, expanding a conflict that had begun in 2014. Ukrainian resistance, international military and humanitarian assistance, sanctions, and widespread displacement shaped the war. The fighting also affected food supplies, energy markets, and European security. The marker identifies Kyiv as a representative location; the conflict extends far beyond the capital.

Q192769.body: Disputes over British taxation and political authority escalated into fighting between Britain and its thirteen North American colonies in 1775. The colonies declared independence the following year, turning a struggle over their rights within the empire into a war to establish a new nation. French military and financial support helped the American cause, while the conflict widened internationally. Britain recognized United States independence in the Treaty of Paris in 1783, creating a republic whose promises of liberty would shape later political struggles.

sources.title: National Park Service — Overview of the American Revolution
National Archives — Treaty of Paris (1783)

Q5599931.body: The rupture traditionally dated to 1054 grew from centuries of disagreement between the Greek-speaking and Latin-speaking churches over authority, doctrine, and religious practice. Exchanges of excommunication in Constantinople became a landmark in the separation of Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Christianity. The division developed over time rather than in a single decisive moment, and later conflicts deepened it. The schism reshaped religious institutions and political relationships across Europe and the eastern Mediterranean.

sources.title: East–West Schism — background and references
Wikidata — East–West Schism

Q232572.body: Emperor Constantine convened Christian bishops at Nicaea in 325 to address divisions within the church. Their debates focused especially on the relationship between Jesus Christ and God the Father, producing the first form of the Nicene Creed. The council also addressed church discipline and the observance of Easter. Its decisions became a foundation for later Christian doctrine, while the gathering established an influential model for councils called to resolve disputes across the church.

sources.title: First Council of Nicaea — background and references
Wikidata — First Council of Nicaea

Q15042830.body: Across the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, Enlightenment thinkers applied reason, observation, and debate to questions of government, religion, science, and society. Books, salons, academies, and expanding print networks carried arguments about liberty, toleration, and political authority across borders. These ideas helped shape reform movements and revolutions, although thinkers disagreed about their meaning and application. The date marks an approximate period of intellectual change rather than a single event or founding moment.

sources.title: Age of Enlightenment — background and references
Wikidata — Age of Enlightenment

Q841211.body: After Attila’s death, rivalries among his successors and resistance from subject peoples weakened Hunnic power. At Nedao, traditionally dated to 454, forces led by the Gepid ruler Ardaric defeated an army associated with Attila’s son Ellac. The battle became a turning point in the fragmentation of the Hunnic empire in Europe. Its precise location and aspects of the surviving account remain uncertain, so the marker represents the wider Pannonian region.

sources.title: University of Leeds research — Hunnic succession and Nedao

Q3849563.body: A Khwarazmian army captured Jerusalem in 1244, ending the renewed period of Christian control that had followed the diplomatic settlement of the Sixth Crusade. The city’s loss was part of a wider struggle among regional rulers and crusader states in the eastern Mediterranean. It demonstrated how fragile control obtained through negotiation could be when military alliances shifted. The milestone marks the conquest of Jerusalem itself, rather than the whole regional campaign.

sources.title: Siege of Jerusalem (1244) — background and references

Q1059658.body: German forces occupied Hungary on March 19, 1944, as Nazi leaders sought to keep their ally from leaving the war. The occupation brought a more compliant government to power and sharply intensified persecution of Hungary’s Jews. German officials and Hungarian authorities subsequently organized mass deportations, many to Auschwitz. The invasion therefore marked both a loss of Hungarian political autonomy and a catastrophic escalation of the Holocaust in the country.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum — The Holocaust in Hungary

Q169390.title: Britain passes the Slavery Abolition Act
Q169390.body: Britain’s Parliament passed the Slavery Abolition Act in 1833 after sustained resistance by enslaved people and campaigning by abolitionists. The act took effect in 1834 across much of the British Empire, but many people were forced into an apprenticeship system that continued until 1838. Compensation went to former slave owners rather than those who had been enslaved. The legislation was a major step toward emancipation, while leaving profound inequalities and colonial systems of coercion in place.

sources.title: UK National Archives — The 1833 Act and compensation

Q3944788.body: In April 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first image of a black hole’s shadow, surrounded by glowing material in the galaxy Messier 87. Researchers combined observations from radio telescopes around the world to create a virtual instrument the size of Earth. The result provided a new way to test ideas about gravity under extreme conditions. It also demonstrated how international coordination and large-scale data analysis could reveal objects previously beyond direct imaging.

sources.title: Event Horizon Telescope — First black hole image

Q7328.body: Vasco da Gama’s fleet reached Calicut on India’s southwestern coast in 1498 after sailing around southern Africa and across the Indian Ocean. The voyage connected Europe directly to maritime trade routes already used by African, Arab, Indian, and Asian merchants. It opened a new phase of Portuguese commercial and military expansion in the region. The achievement was a European navigational milestone within a much older, internationally connected Indian Ocean trading world.

sources.title: Vasco da Gama — background and references

Q7333.body: Beginning in 1405, fleets commanded by Zheng He carried Ming China’s envoys, goods, and military power through the Indian Ocean. Their voyages connected Chinese ports with Southeast Asia, South Asia, the Arabian Peninsula, and eastern Africa. Diplomacy and trade were central purposes, alongside displays of imperial authority. The expeditions illustrate the scale of maritime connections before European oceanic expansion and the influence that state-sponsored voyages could exert on distant trading networks.

sources.title: Zheng He — background and references
